database_summary: This SQLite catalog contains a mix of transactional/event tables (web_orders, web_events, hardware_fact_sales_monthly), dimensional/descriptive tables (hardware_dim_customer, hardware_dim_product, web_accounts, web_sales_reps, web_region, university_* tables), and smaller fact/measure tables for product pricing/costs and deductions (hardware_fact_gross_price, hardware_fact_manufacturing_cost, hardware_fact_pre_invoice_deductions). Row counts show the largest table is hardware_fact_sales_monthly (971,631 rows), mid-size event tables web_events (9,073) and web_orders (6,912), many small reference/dimension tables (tens to hundreds of rows). Several tables use natural keys rather than explicit primary key constraints in the DDL. Time-like columns exist (occurred_at, date, EventDate/EventTime, OffYear/OffTerm). Be cautious joining facts to dims because joins can multiply rows when linking monthly sales to product/customer or when joining sales reps/accounts to events/orders.

accepted.name: dim_customer_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_code,
  customer,
  platform,
  channel,
  market,
  sub_zone,
  region
FROM hardware_dim_customer
accepted.description: Cleaned/passed-through customer dimension. Use when joining sales or deduction facts to customer descriptive attributes (market, region, platform, channel). Preserves original customer_code key and canonicalizes NULLs. | Use for: Aggregate sales by market/region/platform; Filter customers by channel or platform; Join customer attributes to monthly sales, deductions, or prices

accepted.name: dim_product_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_code,
  division,
  segment,
  category,
  product,
  variant
FROM hardware_dim_product
accepted.description: Product dimension pass-through. Use when analyzing product-level measures (price, cost, sales) by division/segment/category/variant. | Use for: Roll up sales/cost/price by product category or segment; Filter products by variant or division; Enrich monthly sales with product attributes

accepted.name: fact_sales_monthly_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.date,
  s.product_code,
  s.customer_code,
  s.sold_quantity,
  s.fiscal_year,
  c.customer AS customer,
  c.platform AS platform,
  c.channel AS channel,
  c.market AS market,
  c.sub_zone AS sub_zone,
  c.region AS region,
  p.division AS division,
  p.segment AS segment,
  p.category AS category,
  p.product AS product,
  p.variant AS variant
FROM hardware_fact_sales_monthly s
LEFT JOIN hardware_dim_customer c
  ON s.customer_code = c.customer_code
LEFT JOIN hardware_dim_product p
  ON s.product_code = p.product_code
accepted.description: Monthly sales fact joined to customer and product dimensions and fiscal year exposed. Useful as the starting wide relation for revenue/quantity analyses by customer/product attributes. | Use for: Compute total sold_quantity by market/region/category; Filter monthly sales for customers or products with particular attributes; Join to price/cost facts to compute margin per product/customer

accepted.name: fact_monthly_sales_by_fiscal
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_code,
  customer_code,
  fiscal_year,
  SUM(sold_quantity) AS total_sold_quantity,
  COUNT(*) AS months_reported
FROM hardware_fact_sales_monthly
GROUP BY product_code, customer_code, fiscal_year
accepted.description: Aggregated monthly sales measures rolled up to product_code x customer_code x fiscal_year. Provides total sold quantity per fiscal year and preserved keys for joining to yearly pricing/cost/deductions. | Use for: Annual sales volume per product or customer; Join annual sales to annual price/cost/deduction tables; Compute year-over-year changes in sold quantity

accepted.name: dim_accounts_with_reps
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.id,
  a.name,
  a.website,
  a.lat,
  a.long,
  a.primary_poc,
  a.sales_rep_id,
  r.name AS region_name,
  s.name AS sales_rep_name
FROM web_accounts a
LEFT JOIN web_sales_reps s
  ON a.sales_rep_id = s.id
LEFT JOIN web_region r
  ON s.region_id = r.id
accepted.description: Accounts enriched with sales rep and region names. Use when relating web orders or events to account-level sales representative and region data. | Use for: Order/event counts by sales rep or region; Map accounts by lat/long and sales rep; Filter accounts for CRM follow-up by sales rep

accepted.name: orders_timeseries_measures
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  date(substr(occurred_at,1,10)) AS occurred_date,
  account_id,
  SUM(standard_qty) AS sum_standard_qty,
  SUM(gloss_qty) AS sum_gloss_qty,
  SUM(poster_qty) AS sum_poster_qty,
  SUM(total) AS sum_total_qty,
  SUM(standard_amt_usd) AS sum_standard_amt_usd,
  SUM(gloss_amt_usd) AS sum_gloss_amt_usd,
  SUM(poster_amt_usd) AS sum_poster_amt_usd,
  SUM(total_amt_usd) AS sum_total_amt_usd,
  COUNT(*) AS orders_count
FROM web_orders
GROUP BY occurred_date, account_id
accepted.description: Orders aggregated at date (day) level with revenue and quantity measures. Useful for time-series analysis, trends, and joining to account attributes. | Use for: Daily revenue/time-series per account; Trend analysis of quantity types (standard/gloss/poster); Join daily orders to account or region attributes

accepted.name: staff_event_intervals
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  StaffMember,
  EventDate,
  EventTime AS event_time,
  EventType,
  -- combine date and time into an ISO-like timestamp for ordering
  datetime(EventDate || ' ' || EventTime) AS event_ts,
  LAG(EventType) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffMember, EventDate ORDER BY datetime(EventDate || ' ' || EventTime)) AS prev_event_type,
  LAG(datetime(EventDate || ' ' || EventTime)) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffMember, EventDate ORDER BY datetime(EventDate || ' ' || EventTime)) AS prev_event_ts,
  CASE
    WHEN EventType = 'Exit' AND LAG(EventType) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffMember, EventDate ORDER BY datetime(EventDate || ' ' || EventTime)) = 'Enter'
    THEN (strftime('%s', datetime(EventDate || ' ' || EventTime)) - strftime('%s', LAG(datetime(EventDate || ' ' || EventTime)) OVER (PARTITION BY StaffMember, EventDate ORDER BY datetime(EventDate || ' ' || EventTime))))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS interval_seconds
FROM StaffHours
accepted.description: Pairs Enter/Exit events into intervals per StaffMember and EventDate using LAG/LEAD. Exposes interval start/end and duration (seconds). Useful for computing worked hours or session durations. | Use for: Compute total worked seconds per staff per day; Identify unmatched Enter or Exit events; Analyze session length distributions

accepted.name: faculty_salary_roster
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  FacNo,
  FacFirstName,
  FacLastName,
  FacCity,
  FacState,
  FacDept,
  FacRank,
  FacSalary,
  FacSupervisor,
  date(FacHireDate) AS FacHireDate,
  FacZipCode
FROM university_faculty
accepted.description: Faculty roster with hire date parsed and salary exposed. Use when analyzing salary distributions by department, rank, or hire date. | Use for: Average salary by FacDept or FacRank; Hire-date based tenure or service calculations; Supervisor hierarchy joins

accepted.name: course_offering_enrollments
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.OfferNo,
  e.StdNo,
  e.EnrGrade,
  o.CourseNo,
  o.OffTerm,
  o.OffYear,
  o.OffLocation,
  o.OffTime,
  o.FacNo,
  o.OffDays,
  c.CrsDesc,
  c.CrsUnits
FROM university_enrollment e
LEFT JOIN university_offering o
  ON e.OfferNo = o.OfferNo
LEFT JOIN university_course c
  ON o.CourseNo = c.CourseNo
accepted.description: Enrollment bridge joined to offering and course metadata. One row per enrollment (OfferNo x StdNo) with course and offering attributes exposed for term/year analyses. | Use for: Grade distributions by course/term/year; Student transcripts or performance over offerings; Instructor load by offering/year

accepted.name: product_price_cost_yearly
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.product_code,
  gp.fiscal_year AS fiscal_year,
  gp.gross_price AS gross_price,
  mc.manufacturing_cost AS manufacturing_cost
FROM hardware_fact_gross_price gp
LEFT JOIN hardware_fact_manufacturing_cost mc
  ON gp.product_code = mc.product_code
  AND gp.fiscal_year = mc.cost_year
LEFT JOIN hardware_dim_product p
  ON gp.product_code = p.product_code
accepted.description: Yearly product-level price and manufacturing cost joined together. Use when computing per-unit margin by product and year after joining to sales aggregates. | Use for: Compute per-unit margin = gross_price - manufacturing_cost; Price and cost trend analysis by product and fiscal_year; Join to annual sales to compute gross margin dollars

accepted.name: pre_invoice_deductions_by_customer_year
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_code,
  fiscal_year,
  pre_invoice_discount_pct
FROM hardware_fact_pre_invoice_deductions
accepted.description: Per-customer per-year pre-invoice discount percentages. Use to apply discount rates to annual sales when computing net revenue. | Use for: Apply pre-invoice discounts to annual sales by customer; Analyze discount rates by customer or market

accepted.name: web_events_daily_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  date(substr(occurred_at,1,10)) AS occurred_date,
  account_id,
  channel,
  COUNT(*) AS events_count
FROM web_events
GROUP BY occurred_date, account_id, channel
accepted.description: Daily counts of web events by account and channel. Useful for activity trends and joining to accounts or sales performance. | Use for: Daily activity per account/channel; Correlate events to orders by date/account

accepted.name: student_transcript_view
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.StdNo,
  s.StdFirstName,
  s.StdLastName,
  e.OfferNo,
  o.CourseNo,
  c.CrsDesc,
  o.OffTerm,
  o.OffYear,
  o.FacNo,
  e.EnrGrade
FROM university_enrollment e
LEFT JOIN university_student s
  ON e.StdNo = s.StdNo
LEFT JOIN university_offering o
  ON e.OfferNo = o.OfferNo
LEFT JOIN university_course c
  ON o.CourseNo = c.CourseNo
accepted.description: Student enrollments joined to offerings and courses and optional faculty. One row per enrollment with course, offering, and instructor (FacNo) information and grade. | Use for: Compute GPA or grade distributions for a student; List courses taken by student with offering term/year; Aggregate student performance by instructor or course

accepted.name: web_orders_ranked
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  account_id,
  occurred_at,
  standard_qty,
  gloss_qty,
  poster_qty,
  total,
  standard_amt_usd,
  gloss_amt_usd,
  poster_amt_usd,
  total_amt_usd,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY datetime(occurred_at) DESC) AS rn_by_account
FROM web_orders
accepted.description: Orders with row_number per account by occurred_at descending. Exposes row_number to support selecting most recent N orders per account downstream. | Use for: Select recent orders per account (WHERE rn_by_account <= K); Analyze order recency and frequency per account
